findings.title: Complex conditional type `TakeTwo` introduced
findings.body: A 19-line conditional type `TakeTwo` was added to handle tuple length variations. This type is non-obvious and hard to maintain. The surrounding codebase does not use such complex types, and the same behavior can be achieved with simpler runtime checks or existing utility types.

findings.title: Complex conditional type `StoreSetStateWithAction` introduced
findings.body: The new `StoreSetStateWithAction` type is a 9-line conditional type that infers the shape of `setState` arguments. This increases complexity and deviates from the simpler patterns used elsewhere in the file. The previous implementation was clearer and more maintainable.

findings.title: New `Devtools` type alias introduced with complex generics
findings.body: A new `Devtools` type alias with three generic parameters and nested conditional types was introduced. This deviates from the simpler type patterns used in the rest of the file and adds cognitive overhead without clear benefit.

findings.title: New `DevtoolsImpl` type and `PopArgument` helper introduced
findings.body: The `DevtoolsImpl` type and `PopArgument` helper are complex and not idiomatic for this codebase. The previous implementation was more straightforward and easier to understand. These additions increase maintenance burden.

findings.title: `NamedSet` type redefined with `WithDevtools`
findings.body: The `NamedSet` type was redefined to use `WithDevtools<StoreApi<T>>['setState']`, which is less clear than the previous direct type definition. This change deviates from the existing naming and type patterns in the file.

findings.title: Complex implementation function `devtoolsImpl` introduced
findings.body: The new `devtoolsImpl` function is a 15-line arrow function with complex generics and nested logic. This deviates from the simpler function patterns used in the rest of the file and reduces readability. The previous implementation was more straightforward.

findings.title: Type assertion `(api.setState as NamedSet<S>)` used
findings.body: The code uses a type assertion `(api.setState as NamedSet<S>)`, which bypasses TypeScript's type safety. This is a deviation from the safer patterns used elsewhere in the file and introduces potential runtime risks.

summary.problem: The refactor introduces complex conditional types, type aliases, and implementation functions that reduce readability and deviate from the existing codebase patterns.
summary.done_well: The new implementation maintains the same public API and functionality, ensuring backward compatibility. Error handling for missing devtools extension is preserved.
